text:
kai: Heads up — bringing up hf/gptq-wf-1.3b-8bit on staging. Streaming answers are truncating early for a few prompts. Looks like the model emits multiple EOS tokens in a row and our client treats the first EOS as terminal. Repro below.

kai: ```
prompt: "Write a haiku about compilers"
model token ids emitted (chunks): [..., 50256]
stream chunk 1: "Write a haiku about compilers:"
stream chunk 2: "Optimizing code
Fast passes, clever inlines
Bugs left behind"
stream chunk 3: "\u00e2\u0080\u009c\u00e2\u0080\u009d"  # shows up as <|endoftext|> in tokenizer
stream chunk 4: "\u00e2\u0080\u009c\u00e2\u0080\u009d"
```

aj: Did we set config.json eos_token_id to 50256 during conversion? HF original has eos=50256 but our converted config sometimes ends up with null.

kai: I inspected the converted model bundle — config.json has "eos_token_id": null. The HF model config had 50256. Our hf->redwood conversion step seems to mishandle models that include both `eos_token` in special_tokens_map and also list entries in `additional_special_tokens`. The converter picks up the list and fails to populate eos_token_id properly.

maria: Checking the tokenizer: special_tokens_map: {"eos_token": ""}, additional_special_tokens: [""] — duplicate entries. Streaming stop logic currently checks `if token_id == config.eos_token_id: finish()` AND also string stop_sequences against emitted text. Mismatch between id-based vs text-based detection may be the root.

sam: Proposed fixes: normalize special tokens during conversion: 1) dedupe additional_special_tokens; 2) if eos_token_id is None but tokenizer has eos_token text, use tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids([eos_text]) and set eos_token_id to the first non-unknown id; 3) add a small guard in streaming to ignore consecutive eos ids within the same micro-batch (treat duplicates as noise).

kai: Quick local check: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/gptq-wf-1.3b'); print(t.special_tokens_map, t.additional_special_tokens, t.convert_tokens_to_ids(['']))"` printed `{'eos_token': ''} [''] [50256, 50256]` — so the tokenizer maps the same string twice, which is why the converter got confused.

aj: Does the duplicate mapping cause early stop? If both tokens map to same id (50256) it shouldn't change id stream, but if the converter left eos_token_id null we end up relying on string matching of stop sequences in chat templates. In streaming that string may be split across chunks and missed, so client sees an early EOS id and closes.

maria: Also saw a chat_template quirk: some templates append an explicit stop sequence like "" in the assistant role text. If converter leaves both token id and stop_sequence set, we get overlapping stop conditions. Need to standardize: prefer id-based stops in runtime, fall back to text stops only if id absent.

sam: I'll pair with kai to add unit tests: - conversion test that asserts config.eos_token_id is set when tokenizer has eos_token -> id mapping, - streaming integration test that simulates duplicate eos ids in consecutive micro-batches and expects continued emission unless a non-eos token follows the duplicate.

kai: I'll open a PR with the converter normalization + tests and add a small regression eval (haiku-style prompt set) to our bringup checks to catch truncation. cc @sam @maria.

aj: Thanks — assigning to eng-ml sprint triage for next deploy. :thumbsup:
